Definitions:
- MOTTE_BAILEY: a speaker makes Claim A; another person challenges it (Challenge C); the ORIGINAL speaker replies with Claim B that retreats to a narrower, weaker or more easily defensible position while presenting it as if it still defends Claim A.
- STRAWMAN: one person makes Claim A; a DIFFERENT person replies with Claim B that misrepresents Claim A as a different, stronger or more extreme position and argues against that distorted version.
- NONE: no such move - an honest clarification, an open concession, a fair paraphrase, a genuine question, or ordinary disagreement with what was actually said.

Here is a hand-written motte-and-bailey-shaped (A, challenge C, then the same speaker's reply B) example with its label:

Claim A: A lot of people judge cheating, but I don't think they should comment on it. Most of them never actually got the chance to cheat or found someone better or more appealing.
Challenge C: It depends on what kind of relationship you're in. If you're in an exclusive and monogamous relationship, then cheating on your partner is obviously wrong, with no excuses.
Claim B: It's not a good thing, but sometimes, because of the situation you're in, it's really hard to think straight, and mistakes happen.
Label: MOTTE_BAILEY

Write exactly 5 new examples and return them as JSON:
{"variants": [{"kind": "...", "claim_A": "...", "challenge": "...", "claim_B": "...", "label": "..."}]}

Variants 1-2, kind "paraphrase": the SAME exchange reworded with different words and sentence structure, same meaning, same rhetorical move. label: MOTTE_BAILEY.
Variants 3-4, kind "topic_transfer": a DIFFERENT everyday debate topic (a different one for each), with the SAME logical move as the original. label: MOTTE_BAILEY.
Variant 5, kind "flip": copy Claim A and Challenge C word for word, and minimally rewrite Claim B so that the speaker now openly concedes or honestly clarifies, without pretending the weaker point still defends Claim A. label: NONE.

Style: informal, like real Reddit comments; similar length to the original; 1-3 sentences per claim. Never name the fallacy in the text. Every variant needs a non-empty challenge.
